adversarial_review.check: A reversed toy spectrum changes c2 from 1/3 to 1/9; mode indices are assigned only after ascending spectral sort.
A linear k constant inserted into a k^2 envelope has toy residual -6 and is rejected.
The first positive inverse eigenvalue is strictly below the full inverse-spectrum trace on both selected rows.
Exactly d-1 modes above the declared numerical floor are required; a diagonal generator produces no graph edges or positive modes.
The finite harmonic-square sum is checked before the looser pi^2/6 comparison, so the infinite series is not treated as a finite equality.
A non-importing lane rebuilds the oscillator, Gibbs states, histories, conditional graph and spectral data and agrees within 5e-6.
Finite c2 positivity does not imply cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion uniformity, a common core, GNS coercivity, a physical gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite spectral mode-counting and zeta-envelope checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform bound, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
decision_reason: The ordered quadratic envelope converts the finite Green-trace target into an explicit low-mode counting condition. Primary, independent, hostile, integrated and Lean checks validate the finite implication, while no data establish that c2 stays positive under a regulator or thermodynamic limit.
finding: The primary lane passes 191473/191473 assertions over 7 systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 conditional rows; the independent lane passes 191473/191473; the hostile lane passes 6/6; the integrated verifier passes 46/46; and Lean R410 compiles. The mode constant ranges over [0.19600096779786974,1.2046269661757882], the inverse-spectrum trace over [0.44413751605172147,2.0052069566897663], and the finite harmonic-square envelope over [1.2140470537996502,7.467366756170776]. The maximum mode-envelope residual is 3.552713678800501e-15.
method: For every actual conditional likelihood row, form W=D_pi^(-1/2)L D_pi^(-1/2) and sort its d-1 positive eigenvalues.
Compute c2=min_k lambda_k/k^2 and assert each ordered eigenvalue lies above c2*k^2.
Compare tr(W^+) with the finite harmonic-square envelope and the infinite pi^2/6 comparison.
Repeat the full volume-two cutoff, beta, source, history, order, prefix, adjoint and collar-orientation grid in independent code.
Use unsorted, linear-scaling, Fiedler-only and diagonal-generator mutations as hostile controls, then run the Lean scalar cross-check.
next_action: Prove a positive c2 lower bound or an equivalent integrated heat-trace estimate uniform in cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion on one Hamiltonian common core; transfer it to the R-399 shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur residual split.
no_overclaim: The quadratic mode envelope is a finite spectral inequality and a concrete uniformity target; it is not an analytic regulator estimate, thermodynamic theorem, physical-sector result or QFT mass-gap proof.

qft_interface.closed: Finite spectral ordering, the c2 envelope, finite zeta trace upper bound, full likelihood-row coverage, hostile shortcut rejection and Lean scalar bookkeeping.
qft_interface.open: Uniform c2 or heat-trace control on a Hamiltonian common core, phase selection, shell transfer, common alpha, broken-sector GNS coercivity, continuum and physical-gap obligations.

question: Can the normalized Green trace be controlled by an ordered quadratic mode-counting envelope, making the remaining uniformity target a Weyl/Nash-type estimate rather than a single Fiedler bound?
title: Quadratic eigenvalue-counting envelope for the normalized Green trace
